definitions.explanation: A formal, literary word for a teacher or mentor one studies under. Rarely stands alone; it appears mainly in set compounds and phrases about the teacher-student relationship.

examples.english: To look up to (someone) as a mentor.
He looks up to a famous painter as his mentor.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いころ、⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{陶芸家|とうげいか}→陶芸家：20904_tougeika⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{師|し}→〜師：30801_shi⟧{事|じ}して⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: When he was young, he studied under the finest potter in the village to learn the craft.

notes:
⟦{師|し}→〜師：30801_shi⟧ is a formal, bound noun for a teacher or mentor; it rarely appears alone and is mostly found in compounds and fixed phrases about study and guidance.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{師|し}→〜師：30801_shi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{仰|あお}ぐ→仰ぐ：11454_aogu⟧: to look up to (someone) as a mentor
- ⟦{師|し}→〜師：30801_shi⟧{事|じ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to study under (a master)
- ⟦{恩|おん}{師|し}→恩師：12598_onshi⟧: a beloved former teacher
- ⟦{師|し}{弟|てい}→師弟：21880_shitei⟧: master and disciple

WATCH OUT:
Do not confuse with the suffix 〜⟦{師|し}→〜師：30801_shi⟧ (practitioner, as in ⟦{教|きょう}{師|し}→教師：03029_kyoushi⟧ teacher, ⟦{医|い}{師|し}→医師：11851_ishi⟧ doctor), which names a person by their trade rather than referring to "a teacher" as a standalone concept.
